title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Transactions with Clients - Borrowing
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A paralegal is experiencing a short-term cash flow problem at their firm. They ask a long-time, wealthy client for a personal loan of $5,000, promising to pay it back with 10% interest. Is this permissible?
options: No, a paralegal is strictly prohibited from borrowing money from a client unless the client is a regulated financial institution or a related person.
Yes, as long as the 10% interest rate is documented in a promissory note.
Yes, provided the paralegal repays the loan within 30 days.
No, unless the loan is secured against the paralegal's real property.
questions.explain: Rule 3.06 (Transactions with Clients). Borrowing money from a client raises severe conflict of interest and undue influence concerns. A paralegal shall not borrow from a client unless the client is a lending institution (bank, credit union) whose business includes lending money, or a related person.
